body_markdown:
*Fundraise Insider tracks newly funded startups each week and delivers verified[sales leads](https://fundraiseinsider.com/) of C-suite contacts straight to your inbox, so you reach the right people while the funding is still fresh.[See pricing.](https://fundraiseinsider.com/pricing)*


Stability AI has raised $76 million in[Series B](https://fundraiseinsider.com/blog/series-b-startups/) funding, bringing the total the company has raised to $232 million.


The most striking thing about the round is who is in it. Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group and Warner Music Group all invested, as did the games publisher Electronic Arts, putting three of the industry’s largest rights holders on the cap table of a company whose models were once a source of considerable friction with them.


The rest of the list runs long: AMD Ventures, Pacific Alliance Ventures, Coatue, Greycroft, Kadmos Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis Capital, Sound Ventures and WPP, alongside individuals including Sean Parker, Eric Schmidt, James Cameron, Kevin Mayer, Mark Burnett, Patrick Whitesell, Prem Akkaraju and Robert Nelsen. Thomas Laffont, co-founder of Coatue, has joined the board.


The company operates from[Los Angeles](https://fundraiseinsider.com/blog/recently-funded-startups-los-angeles/) , California, and now positions itself around professional creatives working in music, gaming and entertainment rather than the general purpose image generation it became known for.


Its tools are built for particular production workflows across image, video and audio. Generative models including Stable Diffusion and Stable Audio 3.0 reach users through DAW plugins, web applications, APIs and open weight releases, which is a meaningfully different distribution strategy from selling a single consumer product.


Chief executive Prem Akkaraju, who took the role in 2024, has steered the company toward that professional market. The new capital funds development of the creative production suite, a deeper applied research effort, and expansion of the professional services arm.


The round lands in a corner of[AI](https://fundraiseinsider.com/blog/ai-startups/) where the commercial question has shifted from what the models can produce to who is willing to license them. Companies selling into newly funded creative technology businesses can reach decision makers through[B2B software sales leads](https://fundraiseinsider.com/saas-lead-generation/) drawn from fresh funding rounds.
